x: But counting best or possible relay splits and remembering that NZ ex-400 metre Champion Callum Taylor has joined us (and he's been running low 47s in straight races):

Surely he must have been in line for 8000 points again but, sadly, injury struck and we must wait for another year. Callum Taylor - 4 x 400 metres (for New Zealand). Born 25th October 1972; personal best 47.31 ('94); coached by John Powell (Belgrave).

We have never, ever notched up a double here but were this time treated to Dave Nolan carrying a brand new Tilda vest to a convincing ten metre margin of victory, followed minutes later by Callum Taylor's storming run from the outside lane where the opposition did not get near him.
Dave Nolan was back with a bang and it took 46.34 to keep him out of first spot in the one lap sprint where Callum Taylor also picked up 2nd.

Aiming for a fast time at Crystal Palace was Callum Taylor. He clocked his fastest time of the season in running to 3rd over 400 metres and setting a time fractionally outside the New Zealand qualifying mark required for a berth in the Kiwis' Gothenburg 4x400m squad.
A fair old contingent of our number contested the Kent County Championships with New Zealander Callum Taylor making a strong showing in the senior sprints.

Hitting the Belgrave Rankings for the first time, New Zealander Callum Taylor, gained selection for his country's World Championship 4x400m squad. Callum is pictured on his way to 2nd in the 4th BAL match at Enfield.
